A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Delethink research. All 34 pages of each version, including figures, tables, equations, and appendices A–J, support comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original RL training experiments, benchmark evaluations, computational measurements, zero-shot model evaluations, and appendix ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results in Sections 6–7 and the appendices, including benchmark scores and computational measurements.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 and Section 4 retain the same chunked reasoning procedure, textual carryover, KV-cache reset, and policy-gradient training objective.

E1.justification: Both versions use DeepScaleR and OpenMath for training and retain evaluation on AIME’24/’25, HMMT’25, GPQA-Diamond, LiveCodeBench, and CrossWordBench. No task or test scenario changes.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged throughout: the main experiments retain LongCoT-RL 8K/24K and R1-Distill comparisons, while Table G.2 retains Long CoT 32k, Budget Force, and Delethink.

E3.justification: The model configurations, training and inference budgets, decoding settings, AIME’24 checkpoint selection, and accuracy evaluation procedures remain identical, including the settings in Appendix D.

E4.justification: The context/state-size ablations, crossword stress test, LongCoT-checkpoint tracing analysis, budget-forcing case study, and per-problem scaling analysis are retained without changes.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the same sampling and uncertainty reporting, including 256 responses per prompt, 5,000 bootstrap replicates in Appendix D, and the sampling-variance analysis in Appendix I.

E6.justification: Reported numerical values, curves, rankings, and qualitative findings are unchanged throughout. For example, Table G.2 retains 1.5B AIME’24 accuracies of 29.3%, 24.6%, and 37.2% for Long CoT 32k, Budget Force, and Delethink, respectively.

T1.justification: The MDP definitions, policy-gradient derivation, and computational scaling and throughput arguments are unchanged, including Appendices A–C. Equation (2) moves from page 4 to page 5 without mathematical revision.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution bullets, and discussion retain the same claims about bounded state, linear compute, constant memory, and test-time scaling. The new subtitle restates architecture independence already explicit in v1’s Appendix J.

C2.justification: Interpretations and limitations are unchanged, including the initialization explanation, speculative pretraining hypotheses, small-context failure conditions, crossword limitations, and lack of larger-model RL experiments.

D1.justification: The implementation example in Figure C.2, hyperparameters in Table D.1, eight-H100 training setup, and code/model access links are identical.

R1.justification: Section 2, the reference list, and Appendix J retain the same cited works and research positioning. The expanded title does not introduce a new relationship to prior work.

P1.justification: The title changes from 'The Markovian Thinker' to 'The Markovian Thinker: Architecture-Agnostic Linear Scaling of Reasoning', with corresponding running-header updates. Body wording and section organization are unchanged.

P2.justification: The expanded title occupies two lines and causes limited text reflow across the early pages. Running headers lengthen; figures, tables, captions, and appendix layouts otherwise remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v2 provides a more descriptive title but preserves the scientific content, evidence, reproducibility information, and limitations, including all appendices. The title clarification and incidental layout changes have no meaningful net effect on overall paper quality.
